newsitem.title: USA: Mexico resumes U.S. sorghum imports - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Mexico resumes U.S. sorghum imports - USDA.

text.p: Mexico has agreed to allow the resumption of sorghum shipments from Texas, the U.S. Agriculture Department said late Friday.

"The USDA office in Mexico City was able to work out a solution to the problem with Mexican authorities. Effective immediately, Texas grain sorghum is again free to move into Mexico," said Paul Drazek, a senior trade official with the USDA.
Earlier Friday, Drazek said that Mexico halted imports of U.S. sorghum, apparently because of Mexico's fight against an outbreak of the fungus ergot.
"It was a technical issue that was sorted out between our Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service and their Mexican counterparts," Drazek said.
Last autumn, some U.S. sorghum producers complained that Mexican authorities allegedly slowed down processing of permits for imports.
